description:
Start scraping Google Maps businesses and their emails. Returns IMMEDIATELY with a job id; the scrape itself takes 5 minutes to several hours.

Before calling this, confirm the category with mapsdata_search_categories and the region with mapsdata_list_regions. Those two mistakes are the overwhelming majority of rejections.

This spends the organization's Scraping Credits (its lead allowance). Set dry_run to check a request against every rule without spending anything.

min_reviews, max_reviews and max_emails_per_company are optional. Pass them when the user asks for them. The response reports the filters that apply, including the default email cap.

cities.description: Named cities instead of whole regions.

dry_run.description: Validate against every rule and return the plan WITHOUT starting a scrape or spending quota.

limit_basis.description: What total_limit counts. 'emails' stops once that many leads WITH an email are found; leads without one are still delivered and never billed. 'rows' stops at that many leads of any kind. Omit it for the organization's default, which is 'emails' unless the organization used the API before this option launched.

list_name.description: Label for the list. Defaults to the query.

max_emails_per_company.description: Most emails kept per business. Defaults to 5 when omitted.

max_reviews.description: Skip businesses with more Google reviews. Omit it for no maximum. 0 keeps ONLY businesses with no reviews.

min_reviews.description: Skip businesses with fewer Google reviews. Defaults to 0, no minimum.

query.description: An exact Google Maps category, e.g. 'Plumber'. Verify it with mapsdata_search_categories first.

states.description: Full region names, e.g. ['Texas']. Not abbreviations. Use this or cities, not both.

total_limit.description: How many leads to scrape, in the unit limit_basis sets. Read max_rows_this_scrape from mapsdata_get_usage first: a larger request is reduced to the Scraping Credits left, not rejected.

name: mapsdata_start_scrape
title: Start a scrape
